packages.doc:
Annotations for code mutastic tests: [`DoNotMutate`](donotmutate/) to skip, [`DoMutate`](domutate/) to keep what would be
skipped. Read from the class files, so they cost nothing at run time.

types.name: BuiltIn
types.signature: enum BuiltIn implements Operator
types.summary: mutastic's own operators.
types.doc: mutastic's own operators. How each finds its sites and rewrites them is the engine's.

members.name: COMPARISON
members.doc:
In `stronger`: with [`BOUNDARY`](#boundary)'s edge moved and [`REMOVE_CONDITIONAL`](#remove_conditional)'s condition always true
or false, the smallest set of changes whose catches catch every other change of a comparison.
For `a < b` that's `a <= b` (boundary), `a != b` (this one) and `false`. Measured on
mutastic's own code (6 Nov 2026), most of its misses were noise: counters that count up to
their end, sizes compared with a value they never pass.

members.name: OTHER_COMPARISON
members.doc:
In `stronger`: the rest of what a comparison can become, and a condition the other way round,
as `mutastic/negate-conditional` was, which it replaced (6 Nov 2026). A test that catches the
mutants of [`BOUNDARY`](#boundary), [`COMPARISON`](#comparison) and [`REMOVE_CONDITIONAL`](#remove_conditional) catches these too, so in the
defaults their catches would only add to the score.

members.name: RETURN_VALUE
members.doc:
Replaced `mutastic/return-default` (6 Nov 2026), which returned each type's default: a `return
false` already returned it, and `null` is rarely what a method returning a list gets wrong.

members.name: REMOVE_DISCARDED_CALL
members.doc:
A call whose result is thrown away, removed: `list.add(item);`, `map.put(key, value);`,
`text.append(more);`. Its result isn't used, so only what it does matters, as with a call that
returns nothing. A fluent call that returns its receiver is no different: removing
`builder.append(x);` loses the append.

members.name: REMOVE_ASSIGNMENT
members.doc:
An assignment to a local variable that already has a value, removed: it keeps that value. A
declaration's first value isn't changed, as the code wouldn't load without it.

members.name: REMOVE_FIELD_WRITE
members.doc:
A write to a field, removed: it keeps the value it had. Constructors and static initialisers
are left alone, as for every operator, and a plain setter is arid, so what's left is state a
method changes.

members.name: OMIT_CALL
members.doc:
A call that only wraps a value, left out, so the value goes on as it was: the missing
`escape(text)`. Only for the calls the engine can be sure of, as a call that returns the type
it's given can still change what it holds.

members.name: SWAP_ARGUMENTS
members.doc: A call's last two arguments, where they have the same type, swapped: the compiler can't tell.

members.name: LOGICAL_CONNECTOR
members.doc:
`&&` to `||` and back. javac has no opcode for either, so the engine finds the two jumps javac
writes for a condition of two tests joined by one, and turns the first round.

members.name: first
members.doc:
One of the operators whose mutants' ids were fixed before operators were open: their ids leave
the operator out, and stay as they were. Every other operator's put it in, including
[`OTHER_COMPARISON`](#other_comparison), which replaced the negated condition: its ids changed with it.

types.name: Comparison
types.signature:
record Comparison(
    OptionalDouble previousScore,
    boolean sameCode,
    boolean sameTool,
    List<Comparison.Flip> flips)
types.summary: This run against the last one.
types.doc:
This run against the last one.

With the code and mutastic unchanged, a mutant is caught or missed the same way every time
unless a test behaves differently between runs. So a mutant that was caught last run and is
missed now, or the other way round, points at the test that caught it: likely flaky. With either
changed, a flip is just the change at work.

params.name: previousScore
params.doc: the last run's score; none when it had no mutants to score

params.name: sameCode
params.doc: whether the code and tests are byte for byte what the last run had

params.name: sameTool
params.doc: whether the same mutastic ran

params.name: flips
params.doc: mutants caught in one run and not the other

members.name: sameness
members.doc: `same code`, `code changed` or `mutastic changed`: what explains a difference.

members.name: likelyFlaky
members.doc:
Each likely flaky test and the mutants whose results it changed: empty unless the code and
mutastic are the same.

types.signature: interface Filter
types.summary: Decides that a method's mutants shouldn't run, and says why.
types.doc:
Decides that a method's mutants shouldn't run, and says why. A filter acts only on positive
evidence in the bytecode, never on a name alone: one that skips too much makes the score lie,
and nobody can tell.

members.name: id
members.doc: `mutastic:trivial-accessors`: how configuration and audits name it.

members.name: prepare
members.doc:
Sees the whole module's classes once, before any [`skip`](#skip): a filter that judges a method by who
calls it needs them all.

types.name: FlakyTest
types.signature:
record FlakyTest(
    String test,
    List<String> failure,
    List<String> reaches,
    List<String> reachesInTest)
types.summary: What a flaky test's failure and reach say about why it's flaky: the difference between a test that's its own doing (an unseeded `Random`, the clock), which can be made to give the same answer every time, and one that reaches outside the code (the network, a database), where changing the test or the code to get past it would hide what's wrong.
types.doc:
What a flaky test's failure and reach say about why it's flaky: the difference between a test
that's its own doing (an unseeded `Random`, the clock), which can be made to give the same
answer every time, and one that reaches outside the code (the network, a database), where
changing the test or the code to get past it would hide what's wrong.

params.name: test
params.doc: the test, as `com.example.QuoteClientTest#aPriceComesFromTheFeed`

params.name: failure
params.doc: the exception it failed with and its causes, outermost first, by class name; empty when the worker didn't say

params.name: reaches
params.doc: calls the code the test ran makes that give a different answer from one run to the next: `new Random()`, `Instant.now`, `System.nanoTime`

params.name: reachesInTest
params.doc: the same, in the test's own class: its set-up, a stand-in it starts. A test whose own code varies makes its own flakiness, even when it fails on the network: a stand-in feed with a random delay times out by the test's doing, not the network's.

members.name: failedOutside
members.doc:
Whether it failed with something from outside the code: an exception, or a cause of one, from
the network, a database, a channel or a file, or a timeout waiting on one.

members.name: failedWith
members.doc: The exception it failed with, by its simple name, if the worker said.

members.name: outsideCause
members.doc: The innermost cause from outside the code, by simple name: `HttpTimeoutException`.

types.name: Mutant
types.signature:
record Mutant(
    String className,
    String methodName,
    String descriptor,
    int ordinal,
    int line,
    Operator operator,
    String original,
    String replacement,
    Optional<String> skipped,
    List<Integer> copies,
    List<String> operands)
types.summary: One mutation of one instruction: which method, which mutation site in it (counted in bytecode order), and what the instruction becomes.
types.doc:
One mutation of one instruction: which method, which mutation site in it (counted in bytecode
order), and what the instruction becomes. A skipped mutant never runs: the change can't be told
apart from the original, or it's code no test is meant to pin.

params.name: className
params.doc: the class's internal name, `com/example/Pricing`

params.name: ordinal
params.doc: which site in the method, counted per kind of site: every arithmetic, branch and return instruction counts as an instruction site, and every call as a call site, whichever operators apply, so a new operator never shifts the ids of existing mutants

params.name: original
params.doc: the instruction: an opcode, `IF_ICMPLT`, or a call, `INVOKEVIRTUAL com/example/Audit.record(Ljava/lang/String;)V`

params.name: replacement
params.doc: what it becomes: `IF_ICMPLE`, `return false` or `remove call`

params.name: skipped
params.doc: why it doesn't run, `equivalent: already returns the default`, if it doesn't

params.name: copies
params.doc: more sites (of the same kind) that get the same change at the same time: the copies javac makes of a `finally` block, one per way out of the `try`

params.name: operands
params.doc: what the instruction works on, as the source names it (`total`, `100`), when the bytecode before it says; not part of the fingerprint

members.signature: Mutant(String className, String methodName, String descriptor, int ordinal, int line, Operator operator, String original, String replacement, Optional<String> skipped, List<Integer> copies)
members.doc: A mutant whose operands aren't known.

members.doc: The same mutant, skipped for `reason` (`user: …`).

members.name: unskipped
members.doc: The same mutant, to run: for an audit of what a filter skips.

members.name: changes
members.doc: Whether the change is made at `site` (counted in this mutant's kind of site).

members.name: fingerprint
members.doc:
Stable across runs and line moves: class, method, site and replacement, and the operator for
all but the first ones still built in ([`BuiltIn#first`](../builtin/#first)), but no line number, because code
moves during review far more often than it changes. A `finally` block's copies share the first
copy's fingerprint.

types.name: Mutator
types.signature: non-sealed interface Mutator extends Operator
types.summary: An operator a plugin adds, or a rules file describes: which instructions it changes, how, and what a missed mutant's card says.
types.doc:
An operator a plugin adds, or a rules file describes: which instructions it changes, how, and
what a missed mutant's card says. Plugins provide theirs as a `java.util.ServiceLoader` service,
in a jar `mutastic.yaml` lists under `plugins:`.

Each mutant's id is made from its method, its site and its change's label, with the operator's
id, so a change's label must never change once released. A call operator's sites are calls,
counted as the built-in call operators count them; any other operator's are every instruction in
the method, counted in order.

members.name: changes
members.doc: The changes this operator makes at `site`, each by its label; none when it doesn't apply.

members.name: write
members.signature: void write(CodeBuilder builder, Instruction instruction, String label)
members.doc:
Writes `instruction` in its place, changed as `label` says. The stack afterwards must hold
what the original left; a change that doesn't verify is skipped as unviable, never run.

members.name: words
members.doc: What a missed mutant's card says.

params.name: skipped

types.name: Operator
types.signature: sealed interface Operator
types.summary: A kind of change mutastic makes: one of its own ([`BuiltIn`](../builtin/)), or one a plugin or rules file adds ([`Mutator`](../mutator/)).
types.doc:
A kind of change mutastic makes: one of its own ([`BuiltIn`](../builtin/)), or one a plugin or rules file adds
([`Mutator`](../mutator/)). How each finds its sites and rewrites them is the engine's, or the mutator's own.

Operators work on two kinds of site, counted apart: instructions (arithmetic, branches, returns)
and calls. A new operator never shifts the ids of existing mutants.

members.name: id
members.doc: `mutastic/boundary`, `stream/remove-stage`: how reports, rules and `--operators` name it.

members.name: explanation
members.doc: What it changes, and when a test misses that, in plain words: for `mutastic explain`.

members.name: onCalls
members.doc: Whether it works on call sites rather than instruction sites.

members.name: tier
members.doc: Which set of operators it's in: what runs unless `--operators` says otherwise.

types.name: Operator.Tier
types.signature: enum Tier
types.summary: The tiers operators come in.
types.doc:
The tiers operators come in. A run takes `defaults` unless told otherwise; `stronger` adds the
operators that find more but cost more, or need more care to read; `extended` holds the
operators on modern APIs (streams, `Optional`, switch arms, regular expressions, exceptions),
chosen on top of another set: `--operators=defaults,extended`.

members.name: word
members.doc: `defaults`, `stronger`, `extended`: as `--operators` and a rules file's `tier:` take it.

A project's own say over which mutants run: the mutants it ignores by id (from
`.mutastic/ignores.yaml`), and from `mutastic.yaml` its rules, then filters of its own (found in
its plugins, run only when named), after the built-in ones; which operators run, and the

params.doc: production classes loaded with the mutated ones but not mutated: another module's own code, when its tests run over this module's mutants

params.name: outputs
params.doc: what another module's classpath has of this one (its class directories, its jar), taken off that classpath when its tests run over this module's mutants

params.name: tests
params.doc: which tests the build runs

params.name: environment
params.doc: the environment variables the build sets for its tests, beyond its own

members.name: withTests
members.doc: The same project, its tests chosen by `chosen`.

members.name: runningTestsOf
members.doc:
The project whose mutants are this one's, run by `runner`'s tests, as `runner`'s build runs
them: its JDK, JVM arguments, working directory, tests, environment and classpath, with this
module's outputs taken off it and its own code loaded beside the mutated classes.

So is any other module of the `build` on its classpath, as one may use this module's classes:
loaded as a library, it would find none of them. A third-party library is outside the build.

types.name: ProjectSetup
types.signature: class ProjectSetup
types.summary: The setup file a build tool's own code writes from inside the build (Gradle's init script, Maven's extension): a properties file with what the module's tests run with.
types.doc:
The setup file a build tool's own code writes from inside the build (Gradle's init script,
Maven's extension): a properties file with what the module's tests run with. One format, so
every build tool reads it the same way.

Keys: `java`, `jvmArgs` (one per line), `workingDirectory`, and path lists joined with the
platform's separator: `classes`, `resources`, `testClasses`, `testResources`, `sources`,
`testSources`, `dependencies` (the test runtime classpath without the module's own directories).
`outputs`: what another module's classpath has of this one. Which tests run: `testIncludes` and
`testExcludes` (one class-file pattern per line, see [`TestSelection`](../testselection/)), `includeTags` and
`excludeTags` (one per line). `environment`: one `NAME=value` per line. Keys a build doesn't set
are empty.

members.name: read
members.signature: static Project read(String name, Path file)
members.doc: The project in `file`, named `name` in reports.

types.name: Report
types.signature:
record Report(
    String project,
    int jdk,
    List<MutantResult> results,
    int tests,
    List<String> flaky,
    Duration coverage,
    int workers,
    int started,
    Duration took,
    List<MutantResult> audited,
    Optional<ChangedLines> scope,
    List<Ignore> staleIgnores,
    List<FlakyTest> flakyEvidence)
types.summary: A finished run: every mutant's result, in the order they were found.
types.doc: A finished run: every mutant's result, in the order they were found.

params.name: jdk
params.doc: the feature version the tests ran on

params.name: flaky
params.doc: tests that failed in the coverage pass and passed when run again: left out of every mutant's run, so their catches don't count

params.name: coverage
params.doc: how long the coverage pass took, of `took`

params.name: workers
params.doc: how many workers ran side by side

params.name: started
params.doc: how many worker JVMs started: one per worker, plus one after each kill

params.name: audited
params.doc: in an audit of the arid filters, each arid mutant's result when run anyway; the mutant itself is in `results` as skipped, as in any run

params.name: scope
params.doc: the change the run was scoped to, when it was: only mutants on its lines ran

params.name: staleIgnores
params.doc: the ignores whose line has changed since: they no longer hold, and their mutants ran

params.name: flakyEvidence
params.doc: for each of the `flaky` tests the run found out about, what it failed with and what it reaches that changes from run to run

members.name: Report
members.signature: Report(String project, int jdk, List<MutantResult> results, int tests, List<String> flaky, Duration coverage, int workers, int started, Duration took, List<MutantResult> audited, Optional<ChangedLines> scope, List<Ignore> staleIgnores)
members.doc: A run with nothing known of why its flaky tests are flaky.

members.name: Report
members.signature: Report(String project, int jdk, List<MutantResult> results, int tests, List<String> flaky, Duration coverage, int workers, int started, Duration took)
members.doc: A run without an audit.

members.name: whyFlaky
members.doc: What's known of why the flaky test `test` is flaky, if anything is.

members.name: merge
members.doc:
This run's results with `other`'s, a run of other tests (another module's) over the same
mutants: a mutant is caught if either caught it, missed rather than not covered if either
reached it, and covered by the tests of both.

members.name: replaced
members.doc: Workers started again after one was killed for taking too long: never fewer than none.

members.name: scored
members.doc: The mutants that ran or could have: all but the skipped ones.

members.name: score
members.doc:
Detected mutants as a share of the scored ones, from 0 to 100; none when nothing was scored,
which is no evidence either way, not a perfect score.

members.name: coveredScore
members.doc:
Detected mutants as a share of those some test reached: how well the tests check the code they
run, apart from the code they don't. None when no test reached any; the threshold is still on
[`score`](#score).

members.name: passes
members.doc: At or above `threshold`, or nothing to score: with no mutants there is nothing to fail.

types.name: Rule
types.signature: record Rule(boolean mutate, String target, String reason)
types.summary: A project's own decision, from `mutastic.yaml`: skip the mutants in some code, or mutate code a built-in filter would skip as arid, with the reason.
types.doc:
A project's own decision, from `mutastic.yaml`: skip the mutants in some code, or mutate code a
built-in filter would skip as arid, with the reason.

params.name: mutate
params.doc: `mutate:`, else `skip:`

params.name: target
params.doc: a class or method pattern: `com.acme.generated.**` (any depth), `*` (one name), `com.acme.Money#toString` (one method)

members.name: covers
members.doc: Whether the rule covers method `method` of class `className` (`com.acme.Money`).

members.name: written
members.doc: `skip: com.acme.generated.**`, as the rule was written.

types.name: Skip
types.signature: record Skip(Skip.Kind kind, String reason)
types.summary: Why a mutant doesn't run.
types.doc:
Why a mutant doesn't run. Skipped mutants stay in the report with their reason and out of the
score.

params.name: reason
params.doc: in words, after the kind: `trivial getter of name`

members.name: toString
members.doc: `arid: trivial getter of name`, as reports show it: the kind first, so it can be counted.

types.name: Skip.Kind
types.signature: enum Kind
types.summary: What the skip claims: `GENERATED`, `EQUIVALENT` and `UNVIABLE` are facts about the bytecode (an unviable change wouldn't load); `ARID` is a judgement that the mutant isn't worth a test; `USER` is the project's own decision.

types.name: Status
types.signature: enum Status
types.summary: What happened to a mutant.
types.doc:
What happened to a mutant. Reports say "caught" and "missed"; the JSONL stream uses the
mutation-testing report schema's names, so it folds into tools that read that schema.

members.name: CAUGHT
members.doc: A test failed with the mutant in.

members.name: MISSED
members.doc: Every test that reaches the mutant still passes: a gap in the tests.

members.name: TIMED_OUT
members.doc: The tests didn't finish in time, usually a loop that no longer ends. Counts as caught.

members.name: NOT_COVERED
members.doc: No test reaches the mutant's line.

members.name: SKIPPED
members.doc: Never run, for the reason on the mutant: left out of the score.

members.name: detected
members.doc: Whether the tests noticed the change.

types.name: Suggestion
types.signature:
record Suggestion(
    String call,
    List<String> parameters,
    List<Long> inputs,
    List<Suggestion.Instance> receiver,
    String today,
    String mutated)
types.summary: A call that tells a missed mutant from the code today, found by running both: the test to write is an assertion of today's value.
types.doc:
A call that tells a missed mutant from the code today, found by running both: the test to write
is an assertion of today's value. Today's value is what the code does, not necessarily what it
should, so the person checks it before keeping the test.

params.name: call
params.doc: the call as Java source, `new Pricing().discount(100)`

params.name: parameters
params.doc: the method's parameter names, in order

params.name: inputs
params.doc: the arguments, one per parameter

params.name: receiver
params.doc: the instances made to call the method on, outermost first: the receiver, after the outer class's instance it's made in if it's an inner class; empty for a static method

params.name: today
params.doc: what the call returns today, as Java source: `10`, `true`, `"text"`, `throws java.lang.IllegalStateException`

params.name: mutated
params.doc: what it returns with the mutant in, the same way, or `doesn't return`

members.name: Suggestion
members.signature: Suggestion(String call, List<String> parameters, List<Long> inputs, String today, String mutated)
members.doc: A call with no receiver arguments: a static method, or a no-argument constructor.

members.name: receiverTakesArguments
members.doc: Whether making the receiver takes any arguments.

members.name: returnsValue
members.doc: Whether today's result is a value (not an exception), which an assertion can pin.

types.name: Suggestion.Instance
types.signature: record Instance(String type, List<Long> arguments)
types.summary: An instance a suggestion makes: its class's simple name and constructor arguments, `Window` and `[5, 10]`.
types.doc:
An instance a suggestion makes: its class's simple name and constructor arguments, `Window`
and `[5, 10]`.

types.name: TestSelection
types.signature:
record TestSelection(
    List<String> includes,
    List<String> excludes,
    List<String> includeTags,
    List<String> excludeTags)
types.summary: Which of a module's tests its build runs: the test task's or Surefire's patterns and JUnit tags.
types.doc:
Which of a module's tests its build runs: the test task's or Surefire's patterns and JUnit tags.
mutastic runs the same tests, so a test the build leaves out (an integration test, a slow tag)
neither catches nor misses a mutant.

params.name: includes
params.doc: class-file patterns, relative to a test class directory: globs as Ant writes them (`**/*Test.class`, where `**/` also matches no directory), or `regex:` and a regular expression; empty includes every class

params.name: excludes
params.doc: class-file patterns to leave out, in the same form

params.name: includeTags
params.doc: JUnit tags (or tag expressions) a test must have; empty means any

params.name: excludeTags
params.doc: JUnit tags (or tag expressions) a test must not have

members.name: ALL
members.doc: Every test, as when a build says nothing.

members.name: leavingOut
members.doc:
The same, leaving out these test classes as well: each by its name (`RacyTest`, in any
package) or its full name (`com.example.RacyTest`).

members.name: runs
members.doc: Whether the build runs the top-level test class `className` (`com.example.PricingTest`).
